craft_notes: Sthāyin: prasāda-śānta of open doors; vyabhicāri peace at whichever-door counts. Sanskrit-first: tri-vartman (THREE doors — kept three, unranked); yataḥ kutascit (FROM-WHEREVER — vagueness kept: vagueness IS the openness); prāpyate (IS-REACHED — passive kept: arrival happens). Rows: 9 (grace/teacher/scripture triple, order kept, unranked), 1 (‘it is reached’ closes — arrival last), 11 (deixis kept vague exactly where Sanskrit vague). Close: ‘it is reached’. Rupture: comma after ‘scripture’ (doors listed, then the rule). Rejected: ranking doors — killed: no hierarchy per C1; ‘attained’ — killed: passive kept; ‘grace-juice’ literalism — killed: ‘grace's sap’ kept (rasa as sap, transmitted). Read aloud: FROM-grace's-SAP, OR the TEACH-er's HAND-ed-WORD … FROM-wher-EV-er, IT is REACHED.

lines: From grace's sap, or the teacher's handed word,
or the Lord's own scripture — from wherever, it is reached.
l4.sanskrit_cite: tatprasādarasād eva gurvāgamata eva vā | śāstrād vā parameśasya yasmāt kasmād upāgatam

reads_against.argmap: By which doors is arrival reached? → Three entries, one arrival, no hierarchy.
c1_essence: Three doors unranked; whichever arrival counts.
